previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of common variable immunodeficiency, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma status post allogeneic stem cell transplant, and Hodgkin’s lymphoma presented with two recent mechanical falls and increasing fatigue, including episodes of falling asleep while standing. Evaluation revealed pancytopenia and mild acute kidney injury. Imaging of the head showed no new intracranial pathology. The somnolence and gait instability were attributed to polypharmacy from multiple sedating medications, including methadone, clonazepam, pregabalin, and dronabinol. A bone marrow biopsy was performed to evaluate worsening cytopenias. She developed a low-grade fever during admission, but infectious workup was negative, and antibiotics were discontinued. Medication changes included reducing duloxetine to once daily and decreasing sirolimus dose, while discontinuing pantoprazole and ursodiol. She improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with services, a follow-up plan for bone marrow results, and recommendations to evaluate for sleep apnea and review her medication regimen.
